primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic chronic kidney disease (stage 2) in pregnancy with hypertension
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) & NICE NG136 (Hypertension in pregnancy)

medications.dose: 100 mg twice daily, titrate up to 200 mg twice daily to achieve target BP <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if ACR ≥70 mg/mmol)
medications.purpose: First‑line antihypertensive safe in pregnancy; provides renal protection via BP control
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends labetalol as first‑line for hypertension in pregnancy; NG203 recommends BP <140/90 mmHg in CKD

medications.duration: From ≤16 weeks gestation until 36 weeks gestation
medications.purpose: Preeclampsia prophylaxis in high‑risk pregnancy (CKD, hypertension, diabetes)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises low‑dose aspirin for women at high risk of pre‑eclampsia

medications.dose: Continue current dose; adjust according to capillary glucose and HbA1c targets (fasting <5.3 mmol/L, 2‑h post‑prandial <6.7 mmol/L)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review each trimester and after delivery
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control in diabetes during pregnancy
medications.nice_justification: Insulin is the recommended agent for diabetes in pregnancy (NICE NG3, consistent with CKD management in NG203)

medications.duration: Continue if BP remains at target; otherwise consider switch to nifedipine SR
medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive; currently providing modest BP reduction
medications.nice_justification: CCB can be used as adjunct in CKD hypertension (NG203); however, nifedipine SR is preferred in pregnancy

medications.medication: Nifedipine SR (if additional BP control needed)
medications.dose: 30 mg once daily, titrate to 60 mg once daily
medications.purpose: Alternative/adjunct CCB with stronger safety data in pregnancy
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 lists nifedipine SR as safe in pregnancy; NG203 supports CCB adjunct therapy

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP after initiation; reduce amlodipine dose if systolic <100 mmHg or patient symptomatic

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive BP‑lowering effect; risk of hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Titrate each drug slowly; monitor BP and symptoms

contraindications.reason: ACE‑inhibitor is contraindicated in pregnancy (risk of fetal renal agenesis, oligohydramnios)
contraindications.alternative: Stop lisinopril now; replace with labetalol (or methyldopa) for BP control
Post‑partum initiation after confirming normal liver function

contraindications.reason: SGLT2 inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy
contraindications.alternative: Post‑partum initiation if ACR ≥22.6 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²

assumptions_warnings: Gestational age not provided – aspirin initiation assumes ≤16 weeks gestation.
eGFR not calculated (serum creatinine 2.0 mg/dL only) – required to confirm CKD stage and dosing of ACE‑I/ARB post‑partum, and eligibility for SGLT2 inhibitor.
Urine ACR not available – needed to confirm microalbuminuria threshold for ACE‑I/ARB indication and BP target <130/80 mmHg.
Serum potassium not provided – required before re‑starting any ACE‑I/ARB postpartum.
Allergy history not documented – assumed no hypersensitivity to labetalol, aspirin, or CCBs.
Blood pressure readings not supplied – assumed uncontrolled on current regimen, prompting medication change.
treatment_summary: The patient is pregnant with diabetic CKD stage 2, hypertension, and microalbuminuria. Lisinopril must be stopped immediately and replaced with labetalol as first‑line antihypertensive safe in pregnancy. Low‑dose aspirin is added for preeclampsia prophylaxis. Insulin therapy is continued with dose optimisation. Amlodipine is retained only if BP remains at target; otherwise switch to nifedipine SR. Interactions are monitored, and contraindicated drugs (ACE‑I, statin, SGLT2 inhibitor) are deferred until after delivery. Key labs (eGFR, ACR, potassium, LFTs) and gestational age should be obtained promptly to fine‑tune therapy.
